topic: Phrasal Verbs: Going Out and Travel

scenarios.context: A family prepares to board a flight.

speakerA.en: Our plane takes off at six. We must check in two hours before.
Have you got your passport? Hold on to it all the time.
At the desk over there. Let's line up behind those people.
No, we'll get through security quickly, and then we can sit down and relax.

speakerB.en: Don't worry. The taxi will drop us off at the terminal at two.
I will. Where do we drop off our suitcases?
It's a long queue. Do you think we'll miss the flight?
Great. I'm looking forward to a rest.

scenarios.context: Two friends are stuck on a bus on the way to a match.

speakerA.en: Why have we stopped? Has the bus broken down?
Oh no. We'll be late for the match. Should we call someone?
Hold on, the driver is coming back. Let's hear what he says.
Good. Let's ring Dad and tell him not to come out.

speakerB.en: I think so. The driver is getting off to check the engine.
Yes, let's call my dad. He can come and get us.
He says another bus will come in twenty minutes, and we can get on that one.
Fine. At least the match won't be called off. It starts at five.

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about someone they haven't seen for a long time.

speakerA.en: Guess who I ran into at the mall yesterday? Parisa!
She's fine. She's moved back to our city, and she wants to hang out with us.
Yes. We talked for an hour. I couldn't believe how much she's grown up.
Good idea. I'll find out if she's free and ring her up tonight.

speakerB.en: Parisa? I haven't seen her since she moved away. How is she?
That's great news! Did you ask her to come over this weekend?
Let's set up a meeting for Saturday and invite the others.
Perfect. I'll make a cake. Let's make it a small party.

scenarios.context: Two friends have to change their travel plans.

speakerA.en: I'm afraid I have to put off our trip. My dad is ill.
He's got the flu, but he'll get over it soon. Can we go next weekend?
Thanks. I don't want to call it off completely.
Great. I'll let you know on Friday if everything works out.

speakerB.en: Oh, I'm sorry. Is he all right? Don't worry about the trip.
Of course. I'll check if the hotel lets us change our booking.
We won't. We'll just push it back a week.
Fine. Tell your dad to get well soon, and take care of yourself.

scenarios.scenario: A walk in the old town
scenarios.context: Two tourists walk around a busy town.

speakerA.en: Look out! There's a bike coming.
Good idea. Do you know where we are? I think we've gone past the museum.
Let's turn back and head for the bridge. We can stop off at a café on the way.
There's a café on the corner. Let's go in and order some cold drinks.

speakerB.en: Thanks. These streets are so busy. Let's walk away from the traffic.
Wait, I'll look at the map. We should have turned right at the bridge.
Yes! I need to sit down and cool off. It's so hot.
Great. After that, we'll carry on to the old market.
